title: Optimizing Attachment of Human Mesenchymal Stem Cells on Poly(ε-caprolactone) Electrospun Yarns
protocol: Dissolve PCL in 1,1,1,3,3,3–hexafluoroisopropanol to give a 10% w/v concentration.
Electrospin the polymeric solution at 20 kV with a flow rate of 1 ml/hr and collector distance of 20 cm.
Collect aligned fibers on the edge of a rotating mandrel at 600 rpm.
Remove the ribbon of collected fiber with a scalpel.
Cut the fiber into lengths of 3 cm or 4 cm depending on use.
Submerge individual strips in distilled water, remove them, and manually twist until resembling thread.
Briefly submerge the twisted scaffold in distilled water and place it on clean, non-fibrous card to dry.
Place each dried scaffold individually in microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 1 ml of 50% v/v ethanol in distilled water to each tube.
Leave for 24 hours.
Aspirate the 50% v/v solution from the tubes under laminar flow and replace with 1 ml of 70% v/v ethanol in distilled water.
Close lids and leave for another 24 hours.
Repeat using 90% v/v and then 100% v/v ethanol (1 ml volumes each).
Wash scaffolds twice with phosphate buffered saline solution (PBS), leaving them overnight between washes.
Remove PBS and replace with 1 ml of cell culture media.
Scaffolds are ready for use post-24 hours after the last wash.
Measure the diameter of the electrospun yarn using a light microscope and imaging software to determine a mean value.
Assume the yarn is cylindrical and approximate its surface area.
Mix human mesenchymal stem cells and determine their diameter to be 20 µm assuming they are round, leading to an estimated number of cells that could attach to the scaffold.
Under laminar flow, open sterile 6-well cell culture inserts.
Separate shorter rings with teeth from wider ringed bodies.
Position the toothed ring pointing upwards and drape a 4 cm scaffold over its center, ensuring it overlaps on both sides.
Place the wide ring body over the toothed ring and scaffold and press downwards to secure the scaffold in position through the center of the cell culture insert.
Place the cell culture insert with scaffold into the well of a 6-well, low binding plate.
Add 10 ml of culture media to the scaffold.
Under laminar flow, place poly(tetrafluoroethylene) (PTFE) troughs into individual petri dishes.
Add 10 ml of culture media to the trough.
Using forceps, drape one of the 3 cm scaffolds into the trough.
Make sure its length lies parallel to the trough’s longer edge.
Under laminar flow, dispense 10 ml sterile PBS through the bioreactor vessel’s main port.
Leave for 10 min.
Remove the PBS and replace with 8 ml culture media.
Using forceps, insert one of the 3 cm scaffolds into the vessel via the main port.
Close off the main port.
Aspirate the media from a 75 cm2 flask containing hMSCs derived from bone marrow (passage 4).
Wash the cells with 10 ml sterile PBS and aspirate.
Add 3 ml trypsin and incubate the flask at 37 °C, 5% CO2 until the cells have dislodged from the flask surface.
Add 7 ml culture media to inactivate the enzyme.
Transfer this total volume (10 ml) to a centrifuge tube.
Resuspend this cell suspension by pipetting up and down several times.
Remove 20 μl of cell suspension and transfer to a haemocytometer.
Place the haemocytometer under a light microscope and image at x10 objective.
Focus the gridlines and count the number of cells in the 4 x 4 squares in each corner of the grid.
Count for each set of 4 x 4 squares (4 counts per grid).
Repeat the resuspension and cell count three times.
Calculate the average cell count from the haemocytometer.
Determine the volume of media required for cell resuspension to achieve a concentration of 60,200 cells in 200 μl.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 241 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the media from the centrifuged tube leaving the cell pellet and replace with the calculated media volume.
Resuspend the cells and media for an even mix.
Slowly dispense 200 μl of cell suspension onto each scaffold using a P200 Gilson pipette by running the tip along the scaffold length and below the media liquid surface.
Leave undisturbed for 20 min.
Dispense 200 µl of cell suspension through the main port for bioreactor vessels.
Top-up the remaining 2 ml culture media via the syringe ports in bioreactor vessels.
Set the bioreactor vessels to rotate at 9 rpm in the RCCS-4DQ bioreactor.
Transfer well plates with cell culture inserts and troughs to a shaker plate.
Set the shaker plate to rotate at 30 rpm.
Transfer well plates with cell culture inserts and troughs to the shelf of a cell incubator set at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for static culture.
Prepare lysis buffer according to manufacturer instructions for DNA assay.
Prepare 1x TE buffer according to manufacturer instructions for DNA assay.
Prepare DNA standards according to manufacturer instructions for DNA assay.
Prepare cell DNA working solution according to manufacturer instructions for DNA assay.
Remove samples from the incubator after 4 hours and place under laminar flow.
Remove media fractions from all samples and place in separately labelled centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 241 x g.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged tubes.
Add 3 ml lysis buffer to resuspend the solution and break up the cell pellet.
Using forceps, remove scaffolds from samples held within bioreactor vessels prior to aspirating media.
For scaffolds in cell culture inserts, first free the scaffold by cutting close to the insert’s edge using a scalpel.
Add 3 ml of lysis buffer to each scaffold receptacle.
Scrape the surface vigorously for bioreactor vessels.
Remove the lysis buffer and place in separately labeled centrifuge tubes.
Vortex each centrifuge tube for approximately 1 minute.
In a black 96 well plate, add 100 µl of lysis buffer for each sample fraction – scaffold, media, and well (duplicate).
In the dark, add 100 µl of cell DNA solution to all wells containing lysis buffer.
Mix gently.
Include wells with lysis buffer containing no DNA as a negative control.
Include wells with cell DNA solution as a positive control.
Measure the absorbance of the wells using a fluorescence plate-reader with 485 nm excitation and 520 nm emission.
Compare data with the standard curve generated from the DNA standards.
Remove all scaffolds from their receptacles after 4 hours.
Place scaffolds in a new 6-well plate (separate wells).
Wash the scaffolds twice with PBS under laminar flow.
Add 2 ml of 1.5% v/v glutaraldehyde in PBS to each well for complete coverage.
Leave the plate for at least 30 minutes at 4 °C for cell fixation.
Remove the fixative solution after 30 minutes.
Wash the scaffolds twice with PBS on the open bench.
Dehydrate the scaffolds with 50% v/v ethanol in distilled water.
Discard the solution and repeat for 3 min.
Dehydrate the scaffolds with 70% v/v ethanol in distilled water.
Discard the solution and repeat for 3 min.
Dehydrate the scaffolds with 90% v/v ethanol in distilled water.
Discard the solution and repeat for 3 min.
Dehydrate the scaffolds with 100% ethanol.
Discard the solution and repeat for 5 min.
Immerse the scaffolds in hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS).
Remove the HMDS and repeat for 5 min.
Allow the scaffolds to dry.
Mount the scaffolds on stainless steel stubs with adhesive carbon tabs.
Coat the samples using a gold-sputter coater for 2 min.
Place samples within the SEM.
Visualize the cell-seeded scaffolds using a 5 KeV electron beam.
